symptom: `alter page Shop.P { replace grid1 column(C) with { column (Attribute: Note, Caption: 'C') } }` on a grid with no column C: `check --references` "Check passed!", exec "column grid1 column(C) not found — a column is addressed by the attribute or the caption describe prints in it". Found reproducing mendixlabs/mxcli#1512, whose own symptom ("An attribute is required when 'Show' is set to 'Attribute'" after REPLACE) is #1468 and reproduces only on a pre-f5901e24 build, on the microflow-sourced grid.
cause: validateAlterPageReferences skipped every column address on a document any INSERT/REPLACE in the script touched (documentsTheScriptAddsWidgetsTo, computed up front), because a column the script adds could be the one addressed. That includes the REPLACE's own target, so the check never ran for the ordinary one-statement column REPLACE.
fix: Track growth in script order (grown[doc]) and mark it AFTER an operation's targets are checked: exec resolves each operation's targets before running it (cmd_alter_page.go resolveAlterPageTargets), so only an earlier operation can add the addressed column. Test: validate_alter_page_column_target_test.go (replace / insert / caption / drop-before-insert reported; same-statement and later-statement additions accepted); bug test 1512-alter-page-replace-column-attribute.mdl.
insight: For #1512 itself, the cheapest discriminator was a pre-fix worktree build (git worktree add <fix>~1) against seven grids, one per source kind: it reproduced the reporter's two mxbuild messages verbatim on the flow-sourced grid only, which identified the report as #1468 without guessing. A 'could not establish' skip computed over the whole script is order-blind; when the executor resolves in order, compute the skip in the same order or it waives the very statement it exists for. The SET dry run (validate_alter_set.go) still uses the up-front documentsTheScriptAddsWidgetsTo.
